# Adjudication Task — Chapter 487

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃487화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|게이트의 존재를 확인한 뒤 여러 가지 생각으로 마음이 복잡했던 나지만, 적천강의 도움으로 깔끔하게 지워 낼 수 있었다.
  6|
  7|“…….”
  8|
  9|아니다. 도움은 니기럴 거. 얼마나 꼼꼼하게 때렸는지 뼈마디가 쑤실 지경이다.
 10|
 11|뒤늦게 만난 혁무진은 끙끙거리는 내 모습을 보고 엄지를 척 치켜세웠다.
 12|
 13|“이야, 역시 조장님! 그렇게 맞고도 일어나시는군요!”
 14|
 15|“무진아.”
 16|
 17|“네?”
 18|
 19|“좋게 말할 때 엄지 집어넣으렴. 주먹으로 정수리 내려찍어서 엄지 공주 만들기 전에.”
 20|
 21|내 근력이면 압축 프레스 쌉가능.
 22|
 23|엄지 공주가 정확히 뭔지는 몰라도, 흉흉한 분위기만큼은 제대로 전해진 것이 분명했다.
 24|
 25|치켜세웠던 엄지를 잽싸게 회수한 혁무진이 작게 중얼거렸다.
 26|
 27|“맨날 나한테만 난리야. 확 그냥 부상으로 쭉 누워 있었으면…….”
 28|
 29|“무진아, 뭐라고?”
 30|
 31|“조장님께서 무림의 신성으로 급부상! 하셨다는 이야깁니다!”
 32|
 33|“…….”
 34|
 35|혼이 담긴 구라 보소.
 36|
 37|이 정도면 임기응변을 아트의 경지로 끌어올렸다고 해도 과언이 아니다. 문득 애잔해진 나는 혁무진의 어깨를 두드려 주었다.
 38|
 39|“그래. 너도 힘내라. 이번 일로 급부상했던데.”
 40|
 41|“예? 제가요?”
 42|
 43|“응. 오는 길에 저잣거리에서 들었어.”
 44|
 45|혁무진 저 녀석이 여기서나 푸대접이지, 태원진가의 북부 고원 평정을 통해 쾌풍검(快風劍)이라는 그럴듯한 별호까지 얻은 무인이다.
 46|
 47|게다가 나 같은 우량주와 항상 붙어 다니니 자연스럽게 주가 상승의 길에 접어들 수밖에.
 48|
 49|“양민들 대화 들어 보면 거의 뭐, 역전의 용사더라고.”
 50|
 51|“큼, 그렇습니까?”
 52|
 53|“어. 최소 초절정 고수야. 이 정도면 완전 급부상 아니냐.”
 54|
 55|입꼬리를 씰룩거리며 좋아하던 혁무진이 의심스러운 눈빛으로 나를 위아래로 훑었다.
 56|
 57|“뭐냐, 그 불손한 눈빛은?”
 58|
 59|“급부상했다면서 때린 다음 급 부상당했다. 뭐 그러실 것 같아서요.”
 60|
 61|“……아니, 미친놈아.”
 62|
 63|괜찮은 시나리오긴 한데. 아무리 그래도 그렇지 내 이미지가 이 정도였나?
 64|
 65|‘생각해 보면 그간 많이 때리긴 했지.’
 66|
 67|갑자기 동정심이 든다. 얼마나 맞았으면 이 정도 피해의식에 갇혀 있을까.
 68|
 69|애잔한 눈빛으로 혁무진을 바라보던 나는 한숨을 푹 내쉬며 입을 열었다.
 70|
 71|“아냐. 저잣거리에서 직접 들었다니까.”
 72|
 73|“진짜요? 다 걸고?”
 74|
 75|“네 불알 두 쪽 건다.”
 76|
 77|“오. 진짠가 보네요. 드디어 태원진가가 낳은 풍운아, 쾌풍검 혁무진의 명성이 천하 무림에 울려 퍼지…….”
 78|
 79|히죽히죽 웃던 혁무진이 멈칫했다.
 80|
 81|“아니, 잠깐만요. 뭔가 이상한데.”
 82|
 83|“뭐가?”
 84|
 85|“그렇잖아요. 왜 조장님께서 제 불알을 겁니까?”
 86|
 87|나는 태연하게 대답했다.
 88|
 89|“그야 당연히 네 불알이니까.”
 90|
 91|“예? 그게 왜 당연해요?”
 92|
 93|“네가 혁무진이니까.”
 94|
 95|“이게 뭔 소리야 도대체…….”
 96|
 97|표정 한번 볼만하다.
 98|
 99|지금까지 내가 혁무진을 대상으로 걸었던 숱한 내기에서 모두 진다면, 불알이 서른 개쯤 달려 있어도 부족하다는 말은 굳이 할 필요 없겠지.
100|
101|“혹시 하나 떼서 심어 볼 생각 없냐. 혹시 나무가 자랄지도 모르잖아.”
102|
103|“뭘요.”
104|
105|“뭐겠어.”
106|
107|내 시선을 따라간 혁무진이 미친놈 보는 듯한 눈빛으로 대꾸했다.
108|
109|“그런 나무가 있다는 얘긴 처음 듣는데요.”
110|
111|“그러니까 네가 최초가 되는 거지.”
112|
113|“조장님께 양보하겠습니다.”
114|
115|“됐고. 뭐 하느라 이제야 나타났냐? 아까부터 안 보이던데.”
116|
117|수신룡이 쓰러진 직후 우리는 두 갈래로 나뉘었다. 그 과정에서 청풍과 혁무진은 제갈풍을 따라갔으니 꼭 이틀 만에 보는 얼굴이다.
118|
119|내 질문에 혁무진이 손에 들고 있던 그물을 흔들어 보였다.
120|
121|“그건 뭐야?”
122|
123|“물고기요. 계속 포획 중이었어요.”
124|
125|“물고기?”
126|
127|“예. 어제부터 계속 잡고 있는데, 쉽지가 않네요.”
128|
129|어, 그래. 당연히 쉽지 않겠지. 물고기 잡는 게 얼마나 힘이 들겠어.
130|
131|물고기가 펄떡이는 그물과 혁무진을 번갈아 바라보던 나는 작게 고개를 끄덕였다.
132|
133|“그랬구나. 우리 무진이가 낚시하느라 바빴구나.”
134|
135|“장난 아니라니까요. 이놈들이 얼마나 난폭하고 힘이 좋은지, 진이 다 빠질 지경…….”
136|
137|빡!
138|
139|“억!”
140|
141|“진이 빠지긴. 충심을 다해 보필해야 할 직속 상관은 내팽개쳐 놓고 와서 낚시나 즐기고 앉아 있어? 널 보는 내 진이 다 빠져!”
142|
143|머리를 움켜쥔 채 뒷걸음질 치던 혁무진이 버럭 외쳤다.
144|
145|“아, 생각하시는 그런 게 아니라고요!”
146|
147|“이 자식이 어딜 함부로 목소리를 높여. 물고기 잡고 있었다며, 인마!”
148|
149|“낚시가 아니라, 포획이요! 포획!”
150|
151|“포획? 청 소협, 이 새끼 포획해!”
152|
153|“앗! 네, 은인!”
154|
155|주위를 얼쩡거리던 청풍이 잽싸게 달려와 혁무진을 붙들었다.
156|
157|화산파의 신성이요, 검성의 진전을 이은 초절정 고수가 펼치는 금나수(擒拿手)를 버틸 리가 있나.
158|
159|나는 속수무책으로 제압당한 혁무진을 내려다보며 엄숙하게 선언했다.
160|
161|“내일 무림이 멸망하더라도 나는 한 그루의 불알 나무를 심으리.”
162|
163|“잠깐. 잠깐!”
164|
165|“묻겠다. 왼쪽 불알이 네 불알이냐, 오른쪽 불알이 네 불알이냐.”
166|
167|“둘 다 내 건데 뭔 개소립니까!”
168|
169|“솔직한 녀석이군. 상으로 둘 다 떼 가도록 하겠다.”
170|
171|“놔! 놓으라고! 이 미친놈들아!”
172|
173|혁무진의 비명이 울려 퍼진 바로 그때였다.
174|
175|취릭!
176|
177|“양지바른 곳에 묻으면 무럭무럭 자라날…… 엇, 깜짝아.”
178|
179|그야말로 순식간에 벌어진 일.
180|
181|새하얗고 길쭉한 무언가가 청풍의 품속에서 빛살처럼 뛰쳐나오자, 혁무진을 제압하고 있던 청풍이 즉각 몸을 일으켰다.
182|
183|“어디 가! 미미야!”
184|
185|“푸하!”
186|
187|간신히 청풍의 제압에서 풀려난 혁무진이 바닥에 떨어트린 그물을 삿대질하며 외쳤다.
188|
189|“포획! 낚시가 아니라 포획! 직접 보시라고요!”
190|
191|결과적으로 보자면 혁무진의 외침은 무의미한 것이었다.
192|
193|미미가 청풍의 품속에서 튀어나와 그물로 향한 그 순간부터, 내 시선은 이미 그쪽에 고정되어 있었으니까.
194|
195|그리고 눈 앞에 펼쳐진 광경을 확인함과 동시에, 한 가지 생각이 뇌리를 스쳤다.
196|
197|‘산 넘어 산이군.’
198|
199|취리릭! 콱!
200|
201|혓바닥을 날름거리며 그물 틈새를 파고든 미미가 물고기의 아가미를 물어뜯는다.
202|
203|‘저것’을 물고기라고 불러야 하는 건지는 의문이지만.
204|
205|쿵! 푸드드득!
206|
207|새빨간 핏빛으로 물든 눈. 톱날처럼 날카로운 이빨에 성인 장정의 팔뚝보다 큰 몸뚱어리.
208|
209|그리고 꼬리에는, 시벌. 저게 뭐야.
210|
211|나는 눈을 의심하며 중얼거렸다.
212|
213|“……가시?”
214|
215|헉헉거리며 몸을 일으킨 혁무진이 퉁명스러운 목소리로 대꾸했다.
216|
217|“말귀 못 알아듣는 걸 보면 귀는 어두우신데, 눈은 좋으시네요.”
218|
219|“미친. 뭔 놈의 물고기가 꼬리에 가시가 달렸어?”
220|
221|“독문 병기인가 보죠.”
222|
223|“……개소리할래?”
224|
225|“아, 말씀드렸잖습니까. 낚시는 무슨 개뿔 같은 낚시. 포획이라니까요, 포획. 저런 놈을 어떻게 낚시로 잡아요?”
226|
227|“허.”
228|
229|포획. 다시 들어 보니 저런 놈을 잡기에 그것만큼 잘 어울리는 단어가 없다.
230|
231|뭐라 구시렁거리며 걸어간 혁무진이 떨어트린 그물을 들어 올렸다. 이제야 안 사실인데, 그물도 그냥 그물이 아니라 철과 쇠가 들어간 철망(鐵網)이다.
232|
233|“그거, 도대체 뭐야?”
234|
235|“보시면 아시겠지만, 이놈들 이빨이 엄청 날카롭습니다. 어지간한 그물은 그냥 한번 깨물면 잘려 나가는 수준이라…….”
236|
237|“아니, 철망 말고. 그 안에 든 놈들 뭐냐고.”
238|
239|“아.”
240|
241|철그럭!
242|
243|철망을 찢을 듯이 거세게 몸부림치는 ‘그것’들을 바라본 혁무진이 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
244|
245|“일단은 모두들 혈어(血魚)라고 부릅니다.”
246|
247|“혈어?”
248|
249|“예. 눈깔이 핏빛이라서요.”
250|
251|혈어라, 섬뜩한 외관에 어울리는 이름이다. 하지만 나는 저 괴생명체의 정확한 이름을 알고 싶었다.
252|
253|‘기감 발동.’
254|
255|쏴아아아, 띠링.
256|
257|나를 중심으로 뻗어간 [기감]의 물결이 놈들에게 닿자, 시스템 알림과 함께 커다란 몸뚱어리 위로 레벨 창이 떠올랐다.
258|
259|
260|
261|[Lv.5 변이된 송사리]
262|
263|
264|
265|- 새로운 어류를 발견했습니다!
266|
267|- [변이된 송사리]에 대한 정보가 갱신되었습니다!
268|
269|
270|
271|아이템창
272|
273|
274|
275|[변이된 송사리]
276|
277|종류 : 어류
278|
279|등급 : 無
280|
281|제한 : 無
282|
283|설명 : 미약한 마력에 노출되어 탄생한 변이종. 몰라보게 강해진 데다 상당한 독성(毒性)을 띠고 있지만, 막상 요리하여 먹어 보면 맛있을지도.
284|
285|
286|
287|
288|
289|“…….”
290|
291|이게 송사리라고?
292|
293|나는 어지간한 성인 장정의 팔뚝보다 큰 그것을 바라보며 생각했다.
294|
295|내가 아는 송사리 어디 갔냐.
296|
297|‘차라리 여기가 동정호가 아니라 아마존이라고 하지.’
298|
299|우선 물고기 주제에 레벨이 5씩이나 되는 이 괴물이 송사리라는 것에 놀랐고, 존나 세고 독성이 있지만 맛있을 거라는 시스템창의 개소리에 두 번 놀랐다.
300|
301|막상 먹어 보면 맛있을 거라니. 독이 있다잖아, 이 미친놈들아.
302|
303|‘그건 그렇고, 역시 원인은 하나밖에 없겠지.’
304|
305|이건 분명 게이트에서 흘러나온 마력으로 인한 변화가 틀림없다.
306|
307|비록 수신룡이 제 한 몸을 희생하여 게이트의 마력을 대부분 흡수했다지만, 잔여물까지 어찌할 수는 없었을 테니까.
308|
309|그리고 불과 한 두시진 전 직접 확인한 바에 따르면, 게이트는 제 기능을 상실했음에도 미약한 마력을 흘리고 있었다.
310|
311|‘만약에 이런 것들이 천하 곳곳으로 퍼져 나가면 어떻게 되는 거지? 혹시 감염이라도 된다면?’
312|
313|사실 질문에 대한 답은 이미 알고 있다.
314|
315|좆 되는 거지, 뭐.
316|
317|동정호의 지류는 장강으로 이어져 있고, 장강은 광활한 자연 생태계와 수많은 이들이 오가는 해상 교통로다.
318|
319|내가 뭐 환경단체 소속도 아니니 생태계 파괴는 둘째치고, 만약 감염 성분이 있어서 육지에까지 변이된 생물체가 넘쳐흐르면 그때는 끝장인 거다.
320|
321|“……아, 돌아 버리겠네.”
322|
323|“왜 그러십니까?”
324|
325|“은인. 괜찮으세요?”
326|
327|“아니, 하나도 안 괜찮아.”
328|

I looked down at the helplessly subdued Hyuk Mujin and solemnly declared, “Even if the Murim perishes tomorrow, I shall plant a single testicle tree.”

[P77]
“Wait. Wait!”

[P78]
“I ask you: Is the left ball yours, or the right?”

[P79]
“They’re both mine! What kind of bullshit is that?”

[P80]
“You’re an honest fellow. As a reward, I’ll take both.”

[P81]
“Let go! I said let go! You crazy bastards!”

[P82]
Just then, as Hyuk Mujin’s screams rang through the air—

[P83]
*Hiss!*

[P84]
“If we bury them somewhere sunny, they’ll grow nice and strong… Whoa, that startled me.”

[P85]
It happened in an instant.

[P86]
Something long and pure white shot out of Cheongpung’s arms like a streak of light. Cheongpung immediately sprang to his feet, releasing Hyuk Mujin.

[P87]
“Where are you going, Mimi?”

[P88]
“Phew!”

[P89]
Finally freed from Cheongpung’s hold, Hyuk Mujin pointed at the net he had dropped and shouted, “Capture! Not fishing—capture! See for yourself!”

[P90]
As it turned out, Hyuk Mujin’s protests were pointless.

[P91]
The moment Mimi sprang from Cheongpung’s arms and darted toward the net, my gaze had already locked onto her.

[P92]
And as soon as I saw the scene unfolding before me, a single thought crossed my mind.

[P93]
*Just one problem after another.*

[P94]
*Hiss! Chomp!*

[P95]
Flicking her tongue, Mimi slipped between the gaps in the net and tore into one of the fish’s gills.

[P96]
Though I wasn’t sure that thing should even be called a fish.

[P97]
*Thud! Flap-flap!*

[P98]
Its eyes were bright blood-red. Its teeth were sharp as saw blades, and its body was thicker than a grown man’s forearm.

[P99]
And on its tail… Fuck. What the hell was that?

[P100]
I stared in disbelief and muttered, “…A spike?”

[P101]
Hyuk Mujin, who had gotten to his feet while panting, answered gruffly, “You may be hard of hearing when people talk, but your eyesight is excellent.”

[P102]
“What kind of fish has a spike on its tail?”

[P103]
“Maybe it’s a special weapon.”

[P104]
“…Are you going to keep talking bullshit?”

[P105]
“I told you, didn’t I? Fishing, my ass. It was capturing. Capturing! How could you catch something like that with a fishing rod?”

[P106]
“Huh.”

[P107]
Capture. Now that I heard it again, there really was no better word for catching something like that.

[P108]
Grumbling to himself, Hyuk Mujin walked over and picked up the net he had dropped. Only then did I realize it wasn’t an ordinary net, but a heavy mesh woven from iron and steel.

[P109]
“What the hell is that?”

[P110]
“As you can see, their teeth are incredibly sharp. One bite would tear through an ordinary net—”

[P111]
“I’m not talking about the net. What are those things inside it?”

[P112]
“Oh.”

[P113]
*Clang!*

[P114]
Hyuk Mujin frowned at the creatures thrashing violently enough to nearly tear the metal mesh apart.

[P115]
“For now, everyone calls them Blood Fish.”

[P116]
“Blood Fish?”

[P117]
“Yes. Because their eyes are blood-red.”

[P118]
Blood Fish. It was certainly a fitting name for their sinister appearance. But I wanted to know the exact name of these grotesque creatures.

[P119]
*Qi Sense.*

[P120]
*Whoosh… Beep.*

[P121]
The wave of Qi Sense spread outward from me and reached them. A System notification appeared, and Level windows rose above their massive bodies.

[P122]
> **System**
>
> **Lv. 5 Mutated Minnow**
>
> - A new fish species has been discovered!
>
> - Information on **Mutated Minnow** has been updated!
>
> **Item Window**
>
> **Mutated Minnow**
>
> **Type:** Fish
>
> **Grade:** None
>
> **Restriction:** None
>
> **Description:** A mutated species born from exposure to weak magical power. It has grown incomparably stronger and possesses considerable toxicity, but it might taste delicious once cooked.

[P123]
“…”

[P124]
*This is a minnow?*

[P125]
I stared at the thing, which was thicker than a grown man’s forearm.

[P126]
*What happened to the minnows I know?*

[P127]
*They might as well tell me this isn’t Dongting Lake but the Amazon.*

[P128]
First, I was shocked that this monster of a fish was Level 5. Then I was shocked all over again by the System window’s bullshit claim that it was incredibly strong and poisonous but might taste good.

[P129]
*It might taste good once cooked? You just said it was poisonous, you crazy bastards.*

[P130]
*Still, there could only be one cause.*

[P131]
This transformation had undoubtedly been caused by the magical power leaking from the Gate.

[P132]
The Water God Dragon had sacrificed itself to absorb most of the Gate’s magical power, but it couldn’t have done anything about the residue.

[P133]
And from what I had personally confirmed just one or two shichen ago, the Gate was still leaking a faint trace of magical power despite having ceased to function.

[P134]
*What happens if things like these spread throughout the world? What if it’s contagious?*

[P135]
I already knew the answer.

[P136]
*We’d be fucked. That’s what.*

[P137]
The tributaries of Dongting Lake flowed into the Yangtze, and the Yangtze was both a vast natural ecosystem and a waterway traveled by countless people.

[P138]
I wasn’t part of some environmental organization, so the destruction of the ecosystem was a secondary concern. But if this mutation could spread and mutated creatures started spilling onto land, then it was all over.

[P139]
“…This is driving me insane.”

[P140]
“What’s wrong?”

[P141]
“Benefactor, are you all right?”

[P142]
“No. Not even a little.”

[P143]
I answered firmly and turned toward Cheongpung.

[P144]
“Young Hero Cheongpung, how many of these things are there?”

[P145]
“I wasn’t assigned to this area, so I don’t know. But Mimi likes them. They must taste good!”

[P146]
Cheongpung gazed adoringly at Mimi, who had already swallowed a Blood Fish several times larger than her own body.

[P147]
“Eat lots, Mimi!”

[P148]
“…Right. I’m the idiot for asking you. Mujin?”

[P149]
“Yes. We’ve captured around a hundred Blood Fish so far, but we haven’t determined how many more there are.”

[P150]
I never knew the presence of a normal person could be this comforting.

[P151]
I looked at Hyuk Mujin with deep emotion and asked, “Great Hero Zhuge Feng knows about this too?”

[P152]
“Of course. As soon as the Blood Fish were discovered, Great Hero Zhuge Feng ordered the waterway at the entrance completely sealed off.”

[P153]
“What about the Blood Fish that already escaped?”

[P154]
“Well, for now, it seems there were hardly any.”

[P155]
“What?”

[P156]
According to the past I had glimpsed through the *Memory Fragment*, the Gate had opened at least a month ago.

[P157]
Judging by the fact that it was still leaking faint magical power, a considerable number of fish should have mutated by now…

[P158]
“Are you sure?”

[P159]
“It’s just a guess, but they were fighting one another.”

[P160]
“Fighting?”

[P161]
“They’ve become so ferocious that they seem to have lost any concept of allies. They’re probably still killing one another right now.”

[P162]
“…”

[P163]
*Should I be happy about this or not?*

[P164]
Their ferocity made them dangerous, but since they had started a war among themselves and were reducing their own numbers, it was certainly something to celebrate.

[P165]
*At least that’s a relief.*

[P166]
I had just let out a sigh of relief when—

[P167]
“There you are, Young Master Jin.”

[P168]
A clear, infuriatingly sweet voice came from behind me.

[P169]
When I turned, Mungyeong was already standing there, looking at me.

[P170]
“They’re looking for you.”

[P171]
“I’m busy. The grown-ups are working, so wait.”

[P172]
“…I was told to bring you no matter what. They have something to say to you.”

[P173]
“Who?”

[P174]
A murderous Sound Transmission bored into my ear.

[P175]
—Me.

[P176]
“…Oh.”

[P177]
Then I had better go.

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.

- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.

Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

# Adjudication Task — Chapter 487

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃487화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|게이트의 존재를 확인한 뒤 여러 가지 생각으로 마음이 복잡했던 나지만, 적천강의 도움으로 깔끔하게 지워 낼 수 있었다.
  6|
  7|“…….”
  8|
  9|아니다. 도움은 니기럴 거. 얼마나 꼼꼼하게 때렸는지 뼈마디가 쑤실 지경이다.
 10|
 11|뒤늦게 만난 혁무진은 끙끙거리는 내 모습을 보고 엄지를 척 치켜세웠다.
 12|
 13|“이야, 역시 조장님! 그렇게 맞고도 일어나시는군요!”
 14|
 15|“무진아.”
 16|
 17|“네?”
 18|
 19|“좋게 말할 때 엄지 집어넣으렴. 주먹으로 정수리 내려찍어서 엄지 공주 만들기 전에.”
 20|
 21|내 근력이면 압축 프레스 쌉가능.
 22|
 23|엄지 공주가 정확히 뭔지는 몰라도, 흉흉한 분위기만큼은 제대로 전해진 것이 분명했다.
 24|
 25|치켜세웠던 엄지를 잽싸게 회수한 혁무진이 작게 중얼거렸다.
 26|
 27|“맨날 나한테만 난리야. 확 그냥 부상으로 쭉 누워 있었으면…….”
 28|
 29|“무진아, 뭐라고?”
 30|
 31|“조장님께서 무림의 신성으로 급부상! 하셨다는 이야깁니다!”
 32|
 33|“…….”
 34|
 35|혼이 담긴 구라 보소.
 36|
 37|이 정도면 임기응변을 아트의 경지로 끌어올렸다고 해도 과언이 아니다. 문득 애잔해진 나는 혁무진의 어깨를 두드려 주었다.
 38|
 39|“그래. 너도 힘내라. 이번 일로 급부상했던데.”
 40|
 41|“예? 제가요?”
 42|
 43|“응. 오는 길에 저잣거리에서 들었어.”
 44|
 45|혁무진 저 녀석이 여기서나 푸대접이지, 태원진가의 북부 고원 평정을 통해 쾌풍검(快風劍)이라는 그럴듯한 별호까지 얻은 무인이다.
 46|
 47|게다가 나 같은 우량주와 항상 붙어 다니니 자연스럽게 주가 상승의 길에 접어들 수밖에.
 48|
 49|“양민들 대화 들어 보면 거의 뭐, 역전의 용사더라고.”
 50|
 51|“큼, 그렇습니까?”
 52|
 53|“어. 최소 초절정 고수야. 이 정도면 완전 급부상 아니냐.”
 54|
 55|입꼬리를 씰룩거리며 좋아하던 혁무진이 의심스러운 눈빛으로 나를 위아래로 훑었다.
 56|
 57|“뭐냐, 그 불손한 눈빛은?”
 58|
 59|“급부상했다면서 때린 다음 급 부상당했다. 뭐 그러실 것 같아서요.”
 60|
 61|“……아니, 미친놈아.”
 62|
 63|괜찮은 시나리오긴 한데. 아무리 그래도 그렇지 내 이미지가 이 정도였나?
 64|
 65|‘생각해 보면 그간 많이 때리긴 했지.’
 66|
 67|갑자기 동정심이 든다. 얼마나 맞았으면 이 정도 피해의식에 갇혀 있을까.
 68|
 69|애잔한 눈빛으로 혁무진을 바라보던 나는 한숨을 푹 내쉬며 입을 열었다.
 70|
 71|“아냐. 저잣거리에서 직접 들었다니까.”
 72|
 73|“진짜요? 다 걸고?”
 74|
 75|“네 불알 두 쪽 건다.”
 76|
 77|“오. 진짠가 보네요. 드디어 태원진가가 낳은 풍운아, 쾌풍검 혁무진의 명성이 천하 무림에 울려 퍼지…….”
 78|
 79|히죽히죽 웃던 혁무진이 멈칫했다.
 80|
 81|“아니, 잠깐만요. 뭔가 이상한데.”
 82|
 83|“뭐가?”
 84|
 85|“그렇잖아요. 왜 조장님께서 제 불알을 겁니까?”
 86|
 87|나는 태연하게 대답했다.
 88|
 89|“그야 당연히 네 불알이니까.”
 90|
 91|“예? 그게 왜 당연해요?”
 92|
 93|“네가 혁무진이니까.”
 94|
 95|“이게 뭔 소리야 도대체…….”
 96|
 97|표정 한번 볼만하다.
 98|
 99|지금까지 내가 혁무진을 대상으로 걸었던 숱한 내기에서 모두 진다면, 불알이 서른 개쯤 달려 있어도 부족하다는 말은 굳이 할 필요 없겠지.
100|
101|“혹시 하나 떼서 심어 볼 생각 없냐. 혹시 나무가 자랄지도 모르잖아.”
102|
103|“뭘요.”
104|
105|“뭐겠어.”
106|
107|내 시선을 따라간 혁무진이 미친놈 보는 듯한 눈빛으로 대꾸했다.
108|
109|“그런 나무가 있다는 얘긴 처음 듣는데요.”
110|
111|“그러니까 네가 최초가 되는 거지.”
112|
113|“조장님께 양보하겠습니다.”
114|
115|“됐고. 뭐 하느라 이제야 나타났냐? 아까부터 안 보이던데.”
116|
117|수신룡이 쓰러진 직후 우리는 두 갈래로 나뉘었다. 그 과정에서 청풍과 혁무진은 제갈풍을 따라갔으니 꼭 이틀 만에 보는 얼굴이다.
118|
119|내 질문에 혁무진이 손에 들고 있던 그물을 흔들어 보였다.
120|
121|“그건 뭐야?”
122|
123|“물고기요. 계속 포획 중이었어요.”
124|
125|“물고기?”
126|
127|“예. 어제부터 계속 잡고 있는데, 쉽지가 않네요.”
128|
129|어, 그래. 당연히 쉽지 않겠지. 물고기 잡는 게 얼마나 힘이 들겠어.
130|
131|물고기가 펄떡이는 그물과 혁무진을 번갈아 바라보던 나는 작게 고개를 끄덕였다.
132|
133|“그랬구나. 우리 무진이가 낚시하느라 바빴구나.”
134|
135|“장난 아니라니까요. 이놈들이 얼마나 난폭하고 힘이 좋은지, 진이 다 빠질 지경…….”
136|
137|빡!
138|
139|“억!”
140|
141|“진이 빠지긴. 충심을 다해 보필해야 할 직속 상관은 내팽개쳐 놓고 와서 낚시나 즐기고 앉아 있어? 널 보는 내 진이 다 빠져!”
142|
143|머리를 움켜쥔 채 뒷걸음질 치던 혁무진이 버럭 외쳤다.
144|
145|“아, 생각하시는 그런 게 아니라고요!”
146|
147|“이 자식이 어딜 함부로 목소리를 높여. 물고기 잡고 있었다며, 인마!”
148|
149|“낚시가 아니라, 포획이요! 포획!”
150|
151|“포획? 청 소협, 이 새끼 포획해!”
152|
153|“앗! 네, 은인!”
154|
155|주위를 얼쩡거리던 청풍이 잽싸게 달려와 혁무진을 붙들었다.
156|
157|화산파의 신성이요, 검성의 진전을 이은 초절정 고수가 펼치는 금나수(擒拿手)를 버틸 리가 있나.
158|
159|나는 속수무책으로 제압당한 혁무진을 내려다보며 엄숙하게 선언했다.
160|
161|“내일 무림이 멸망하더라도 나는 한 그루의 불알 나무를 심으리.”
162|
163|“잠깐. 잠깐!”
164|
165|“묻겠다. 왼쪽 불알이 네 불알이냐, 오른쪽 불알이 네 불알이냐.”
166|
167|“둘 다 내 건데 뭔 개소립니까!”
168|
169|“솔직한 녀석이군. 상으로 둘 다 떼 가도록 하겠다.”
170|
171|“놔! 놓으라고! 이 미친놈들아!”
172|
173|혁무진의 비명이 울려 퍼진 바로 그때였다.
174|
175|취릭!
176|
177|“양지바른 곳에 묻으면 무럭무럭 자라날…… 엇, 깜짝아.”
178|
179|그야말로 순식간에 벌어진 일.
180|
181|새하얗고 길쭉한 무언가가 청풍의 품속에서 빛살처럼 뛰쳐나오자, 혁무진을 제압하고 있던 청풍이 즉각 몸을 일으켰다.
182|
183|“어디 가! 미미야!”
184|
185|“푸하!”
186|
187|간신히 청풍의 제압에서 풀려난 혁무진이 바닥에 떨어트린 그물을 삿대질하며 외쳤다.
188|
189|“포획! 낚시가 아니라 포획! 직접 보시라고요!”
190|
191|결과적으로 보자면 혁무진의 외침은 무의미한 것이었다.
192|
193|미미가 청풍의 품속에서 튀어나와 그물로 향한 그 순간부터, 내 시선은 이미 그쪽에 고정되어 있었으니까.
194|
195|그리고 눈 앞에 펼쳐진 광경을 확인함과 동시에, 한 가지 생각이 뇌리를 스쳤다.
196|
197|‘산 넘어 산이군.’
198|

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
